title: Gooey
year_note: Single released 14 February 2014; album Zaba followed in June 2014.

notes.made: Dave Bayley wrote and co-produced it with Paul Epworth at Wolf Tone Studios in London; it came out on the Wolf Tone label. The album leaned on William Steig's children's book The Zabajaba Jungle, and Bayley recorded field sounds, animal noises and percussion from cooking utensils and toys. He sang his vocal holding a pineapple he named Sasha Fierce, and for the final chorus he sang eight different character impressions to make a fake choir.
notes.context: The four of them met at St Edward's School in Oxford and formed the band in 2010. Gooey was their breakout, No. 12 in Triple J's Hottest 100 of 2014, and it ended up on the Magic Mike XXL soundtrack and double platinum in the US. It set up the long climb that ended with Heat Waves going to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2022.

listen_for.note: That 'choir' is Bayley eight times over, each in a different voice.

leads_to.title: Heat Waves
leads_to.why: Where the Gooey sound went: a TikTok-era slow burn that took over a year to reach No. 1 in the US.

notes.unverified: No interview I found explains what the Gooey lyric is about. Only one source-backed listen-for note.

culture.title: The Apiary's spit-thread video
culture.line: The Apiary (Lily Coates and Gavin Youngs) wanted sensual with a touch of ick. They cast a father-and-son wrestling team, the father about 70, to pass spit between them.

culture.title: Magic Mike XXL
culture.line: Gooey is on the soundtrack of Magic Mike XXL (2015).

culture.title: Seth Meyers and Letterman
culture.line: Glass Animals played it on Late Night with Seth Meyers in 2014 and on Letterman's Late Show on 24 February 2015.

culture.title: Slow burn
culture.line: It never reached the Hot 100 (No. 20 on Hot Singles Sales, No. 40 in Australia) but has gone 2x Platinum in the US and 3x Platinum in Australia.
